The paper presents a near-zero refractive index metamaterial for electromagnetic invisibility cloaking operation.
The proposed unit cell exhibits a wideband near-zero refractive index property in the C-band region of microwave spectra.
The frequency range of the wideband near-zero refractive index property is from 5.20 GHz to 8.48 GHz.
The effective permittivity was calculated from the S-parameters using the method mentioned in [31].
The normalized scattering width is a measure of the total energy scattered from an object, normalized to the incident energy.
The cloaking effect is observed at a frequency of 5.18 GHz.
The transmission coefficient (S21) touches the free space line at a frequency of 5.25 GHz.
The measured result of the transmission parameter (S21) for the cloaked state shows a peak very close to zero at a frequency of 5.29 GHz.
The proposed metamaterial is designed to operate in the C-band region of microwave spectra.
The unit cell consists of two orthogonal metal arms with unequal gaps, forming a near-pi-shape structure.
The scattering cancellation technique is used to cloak the object.
The cloaking effect is observed in the xy-plane.
The electric field distribution in the xy-plane shows a fine wave front reconstruction for the cloaked object.
The H-field distribution in the xy-plane also displays the same behavior as the E-field distribution.
The proposed metamaterial has a refractive index close to zero in the C-band region of microwave spectra.
The frequency range of the wideband near-zero refractive index property is from 5.20 GHz to 8.48 GHz.
The effective permittivity is negative at a frequency of 8.29 GHz, with ε = −1.15.
The effective permeability is positive at a frequency of 8.29 GHz, with μ = 1.15.
